questionText: Local College Affordability, Job Training, Repairs Measure. To maintain affordable college education access, by repairing /upgrading San Bernardino Valley College, Crafton Hills College; preparing students/ veterans for high-demand careers including skilled trades, firefighting, healthcare; providing safe drinking water; removing asbestos, mold; repairing deteriorating gas lines; acquiring, constructing, repairing facilities, sites, equipment; shall San Bernardino Community College District’s measure authorizing $898,000,000 in bonds at legal rates, levying $25 per $100,000 of assessed valuation ($56,000,000 annually) while bonds are outstanding, requiring oversight, audits, be adopted?

record.whatItDoes: Authorize up to $898 million in bonds for San Bernardino Valley College and Crafton Hills College facilities, career-training and student/veteran education facilities, drinking water, asbestos and mold removal, gas-line repairs, and other listed projects, including a new mountain-community college center. Property taxes on taxable property in the district would repay principal and interest. The district estimates $56 million annually, an average rate of $25 and highest rate of $25 per $100,000 of assessed value, collection through fiscal year 2058–59, and approximately $1.9 billion total repayment. These are estimates that may vary, not guaranteed tax caps or repayment amounts. Interest rates must stay within legal limits. Money must remain local and be spent on the listed facility projects. Bond proceeds cannot pay teacher or administrator salaries or other operating expenses. Independent citizen oversight and annual financial and performance audits are required. Listing a project does not guarantee that it will be completed; costs, available funds and other funding sources affect the final work. Approval requires 55% of votes.
record.yesMeans: Authorize the district to borrow up to $898 million for the listed facilities and levy property taxes to repay the bonds under these conditions.
record.noMeans: Do not authorize these bonds through this measure.

jurisdiction: San Bernardino Mountains Community Hospital District
questionText: To repair and upgrade 75-year-old Mountains Community Hospital including: fixing deteriorating roofs, plumbing, electrical, and safety systems; upgrading/expanding emergency department, medical technology, and treatments; and maintaining local access to life-saving emergency medical care for accidents, heart attacks, strokes, and other emergencies, shall San Bernardino Mountains Community Hospital District's measure be adopted authorizing $61,000,000 in bonds at legal rates, levying $25 per $100,000 assessed value ($3,500,000 annually) while bonds are outstanding, with independent oversight and all money locally- controlled?

record.whatItDoes: Authorize up to $61 million in bonds for Mountains Community Hospital repairs and upgrades, a new acute-care and emergency wing, conversion of the old acute-care unit to long-term care, medical technology, access and parking, infrastructure, seismic work and emergency utility capacity. Property taxes on taxable property in the district would repay principal and interest. The district estimates $3.5 million annually, an average rate of $23.37 and highest rate of $25 per $100,000 of assessed value, collection through fiscal year 2055–56, and approximately $106,182,725 total repayment. These are estimates that may vary, not guaranteed tax caps or repayment amounts. Interest rates must stay within legal limits. Money must remain local and be spent on the listed facility projects. Money is restricted to the listed hospital facilities and eligible project costs; it cannot pay employee salaries or other operating expenses. Independent citizen oversight and annual financial and performance audits are required. The estimates assume that part of the financing receives a low-interest federal agricultural-department loan; that loan is not guaranteed. This property tax would be additional to taxes for other outstanding district or overlapping-agency bonds. Approval requires two-thirds of votes.
record.yesMeans: Authorize the district to borrow up to $61 million for the listed facilities and levy property taxes to repay the bonds under these conditions.

jurisdiction: Rim of the World Recreation and Park District
questionText: Shall Rim of the World Recreation & Park District adopt a resolution increasing its annual special parcel tax from $22 to $37/parcel, with an annual escalator of 1%, until ended by voters, generating approximately $510,000 the first year, to sustain essential recreation services; improve and maintain parks, recreational facilities, and community amenities; address rising costs, emergency repair and disaster recovery; all funds remain local used only for these purposes with annual audit/ reporting?

record.whatItDoes: Increase the district’s annual special parcel tax from $22 to $37 per taxable parcel, with a 1% annual increase, beginning July 1, 2027. The district estimates $510,000 in the first year. The tax would apply to improved and unimproved parcels identified by assessor parcel number; a taxable possessory-interest holder would pay when the owner is legally exempt, unless that holder is also exempt. Revenue must remain local in a separate fund for recreation services, parks and facilities, related personnel and benefits, emergency repairs, disaster recovery and other listed district purposes. Annual independent audits, an accounting and a report on revenue, spending and project status are required. The board could reduce, suspend or restore the tax within the approved maximum and method. The tax has no fixed expiration; increasing its maximum or ending it would require the applicable voter action. Approval requires a two-thirds vote.
record.yesMeans: Approve the increase to $37 per parcel, the annual 1% adjustment and the stated spending and oversight conditions.
record.noMeans: Keep the current $22 annual parcel tax rather than adopting this increase.
